entries.proposition: The model is a conditional deletion of CerS2 (exons 2 to 9 flanked) with nestin-Cre (CNS) and olig-Cre (oligodendrocyte lineage) in mouse; CerS2 is a very-long-chain ceramide synthase. WWOX does not occur in the paper.
entries.snippet: Briefly, the flanking of the 2nd and 9th exon in CerS2 gene was inserted in two loxp sites.

entries.proposition: Brain lipidomics: very-long-chain (C22-C24) ceramides fall and C16-C18 ceramides rise in the CNS knockout.
entries.snippet: As expected, we observed significant reductions in the brain levels of CerS2 and its characteristic products – VLC ceramides (C22–C24), accompanied by compensatory increases in C16 and C18 ceramides (Fig. 1A and Supplementary Fig. 1B).

entries.proposition: Convulsions start about 4 months and mortality rises from about 5 months in the CNS knockout; the phenotype is late compared with the Wwox-null mouse.
entries.snippet: Commencing from approximately 4 months of age, cKO-nestin mice developed convulsions (Supplementary Video 1), with visible damages in the corpus callosum (CC) (Supplementary Fig. 1D). Mortality increased sharply from around 5 months of age (Fig. 1B).

entries.proposition: Behavioural testing of the CNS knockout shows spatial-memory impairment in the Y maze and no deficit in locomotion, anxiety, depressive-like behaviour or social dominance.
entries.snippet: cKO-nestin mice exhibited significant spatial memory impairment in the Y-maze test (Fig. 1C), with no apparent irregularities in locomotion, general anxiety, depressive-like symptoms or social dominance based on the rotarod, open field, forced swim and tube tests (Supplementary Fig. 1E-I).

entries.proposition: Hypomyelination is already present at postnatal day 20 and is oligodendrocyte-lineage deletion sufficient (cKO-OL).
entries.snippet: EM images revealed significant reductions in both the number and thickness (g-ratio) of myelin sheaths in cKO-nestin mice as early as P20.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 2A-C. At P20 the plotted points are two for controls and four for the knockout in the myelin-sheath count (2B) and the g-ratio (2C), whereas the legend states n = 4 for Ctrl and n = 2 for cKO-nestin; the legend and the plotted group sizes are reversed, and one of the groups has two animals.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2B bars Ctrl and cKO-nestin (P20) with two black points and four red points, p = 0.038; Fig 2C g-ratio with two black and four red points, p = 0.007; legend text in the paper reads n = 4 for Ctrl, n = 2 for cKO-nestin mice.

entries.proposition: Lipid remodelling occurs without change in the mRNA of the relevant biosynthetic enzymes, and the authors read it as substrate-availability shift.
entries.snippet: Notably, the substantial remodeling of brain lipidomes occurred without alterations in the mRNA levels of key relevant biosynthetic enzymes, such as UGCG, B4GALT6 (Supplementary Fig. 3D).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 3A-E. Sulfatide, sphingomyelin, galactosylceramide and glucosylceramide species with C22-C25 chains are strongly reduced (in places by a factor of ten or more, triple asterisks), the C16-C18 species rise, and S1P d18:1 falls from about 0.0075 to about 0.0025 umol/g.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3A-E bar charts for SL, SM, GalCer, GluCer and S1P species, control black and cKO-nestin red, n = 7 and 5, with triple-asterisk reductions across the very-long-chain species and a few C16/C18 species higher.

entries.proposition: Spatial lipidomics places the very-long-chain sphingolipid deficit in white-matter tracts.
entries.snippet: These deficiencies were localized precisely to major white matter tracts, including the corpus callosum (a critical region for myelination), as well as external and internal capsules of the brain.

entries.proposition: Cholesterol depletion with beta-cyclodextrin is used to disrupt microdomains and is reported to impair myelination 'severely'.
entries.snippet: Addition of 50 μM β-CD to wild-type co-cultures severely impaired myelination (Fig. 6C), and a higher dose at 250 μM showed no additive effect (Fig. 6D).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 6D. Relative length of MBP-positive neurite segments: DMSO about 1.3, 50 uM beta-CD about 0.8, 250 uM beta-CD about 0.8 (p 0.02 and 0.03; n = 8, 10, 8). The quantified reduction is about 40 percent and flat across doses, while the 250 uM image panel (6C) shows no MBP-positive segments. Beta-cyclodextrin depletes cholesterol; the experiment does not remove very-long-chain sphingolipids.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 6D scatter-bar panel y-axis 'Relative length of MBP+ NF+ neurite segment' with groups 0, 50, 250 uM beta-CD and p values 0.0226, 0.0297 and NS; Fig 6C three images DMSO, 50 uM, 250 uM.

entries.proposition: The authors state that a definitive causal link needs supplementation with purified individual very-long-chain species.
entries.snippet: We acknowledge that a definitive causal link requires supplementation with purified individual VLC species, but this remains technically challenging due to difficulties in isolating specific VLC sphingolipids (e.g., distinct ceramides).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 7B and 7D. 7B: MBP-positive cell rates about 0.030 (control) versus about 0.020 (knockout), p = 0.0256, n = 5 per group, so mature oligodendrocytes are 2 to 3 percent of cells in both. 7D: control-brain lipid extract raises the rate to about 0.085 against about 0.04 without or with knockout-brain extract (p = 0.0001 and 0.0029; n = 29 and 15).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 7B bars 'MBP+ cells rates' Ctrl about 0.03 and cKO-nestin about 0.02 p=0.0256; Fig 7D three groups with and without Ctrl lipids and cKO lipids, p=0.0001 and p=0.0029.

entries.proposition: The authors name the missing in vivo electrophysiology and the constitutive design as limits.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, while our behavioral tests correlate with the structural myelin defects, future studies employing in vivo or slice electrophysiology will be essential to definitively establish the causal conduction deficits resulting from hypomyelination, thereby linking structural defects to functional impairment.

entries.proposition: A human CerS2 case is cited for the clinical connection: progressive myoclonic epilepsy with a heterozygous CerS2 deletion and low very-long-chain sphingolipids.
entries.snippet: The clinical significance of CerS2 is highlighted by a case of progressive myoclonic epilepsy in a patient with heterozygous CerS2 deletion, leading to substantially reduced levels of VLC sphingolipids [22].
